ACER against no treatment for treatment B and its ICER against A

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7001176
Type test case
has calculator text C_i = 10000; E_i = 5.60; C_0 = 1000; E_0 = 5.00; ACER_i0 = 15000

has description in the module All values are illustrative and come from the article's example. https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006545
Type test case
has description in the module When the loss ratio reaches MinLossRate and the loss rate times the total excess reaches the lesser of the two limits, SharedLossBasic must equal that limit; otherwise SharedLossBasic divided by the total excess must equal LossRate; below the MLR it must be 0. Expected result TRUE for every worked example. In the Level C example a cell that uses the revenue-based limit alone returns 4,000,000 and a cell with no limit returns 7,200,000, both FALSE; in the revenue-limited Level D example a cell with no limit returns 2,160,000 and the cell doubled to 3,200,000 or halved to 800,000 gives FALSE. With Spending equal to Benchmark, MinLossRate 0 and a positive ParticipantRevenue the ratio branch divides by zero and the test returns #DIV/0!.
has implementation text =IF((Spending-Benchmark)/Benchmark<MinLossRate,SharedLossBasic=0,IF(LossRate*Beneficiaries*(Spending-Benchmark)>=MIN(RevLimitShare*ParticipantRevenue,BmkLimitShare*Beneficiaries*Benchmark),ABS(SharedLossBasic-MIN(RevLimitShare*ParticipantRevenue,BmkLimitShare*Beneficiaries*Benchmark))<1,ABS(SharedLossBasic/(Beneficiaries*(Spending-Benchmark))-LossRate)<1E-6))
has module record identifier HE-VT-ACO-004
has test kind identity check
has title in the module BASIC shared losses equal the loss rate on the whole excess or the recoupment limit
has title key basic-shared-losses-equal-the-loss-rate-on-the-whole-excess-or-the-recoupment-limit

Closed-form EVSI plus the current value equals the unit normal loss integral

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7003622
Type test case
has description in the module EVSI in a cell named EVSIPerPerson plus the larger of m0 and zero equals the expected maximum of the posterior mean and zero, m0 times 1 minus Phi(minus m0 over s) plus s times phi(minus m0 over s), the unit normal loss integral in the form given by Lee and colleagues. Expected result TRUE for either sign of m0. FALSE shows the absolute value omitted when m0 is negative or Phi(z) used where 1 minus Phi(z) belongs.

has description in the module The spreadsheet formula of Fuller and Lury sums p_t L_(t+1) minus p_(t+1) L_t over adjacent groups, where p_t is the cumulative population share and L_t the cumulative share of health up to group t.
